claims.text: The base alloy has composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Adding approximately 2–4 at.% boron is the proposed intervention.
A minor boron addition will suppress primary crystalline nucleation during cooling.
A minor boron addition will suppress crystallization during annealing or reheating.
Slow cooling at approximately 52 K/s produces a complex crystalline microstructure in the unmodified alloy.
Slow cooling produces several primary crystalline phases in the unmodified alloy.
Rapid quenching at 10^5–10^6 K/s by melt spinning yields an amorphous structure in the unmodified alloy.
Accelerated cooling at 3018 K/s produces fewer phases than slow cooling.
Phosphorus and high mixing entropy enhance the glass-forming ability of the unmodified alloy.
Boron atoms increase atomic-level disorder in the alloy.
Boron raises the viscosity of the melt.
Boron hinders the atomic ordering required for crystal formation.
Boron increases the nucleation energy barrier.
Increasing the nucleation barrier will delay or prevent primary crystallization during cooling and reheating.
The boron-modified alloy will retain a larger amorphous fraction than the unmodified alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will have a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature than the unmodified alloy.
Boron addition will reduce formation of primary crystalline phases.
The unmodified alloy forms FCC, tetragonal, and orthorhombic phases under slow cooling.
A nearly 365 K crystallization-temperature shift, from approximately 1706 K to 1341 K, was previously observed.
The intervention is intended to operate across cooling rates from approximately 52 K/s to 10^5–10^6 K/s and during subsequent DSC reheating.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome calls for a higher crystallization-onset temperature, while the cited comparison is a downward shift from about 1706 K to 1341 K. The hypothesis does not clearly distinguish cooling crystallization/undercooling from the DSC reheating onset, making the claimed direction internally inconsistent or ambiguous.
